subject: Dedicated capacity: QoS & throughput plan + next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kate Reynolds <kate.reynolds@novabank.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 09:32:00 -0500
Subject: Dedicated capacity: QoS & throughput plan + next steps

Hi Kate — great conversation this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap and immediate next steps from our side so we keep momentum: 

Summary of discovery items:
- Primary workload: customer-facing chat + document Q&A (structured outputs + tool calling for payments lookup).
- Peak concurrency: ~420 concurrent sessions during peak windows (09:00–11:00 ET), baseline 80–120 outside peak.
- Avg prompt length: 120 tokens in, expecting ~400 tokens out (structured JSON for tools).
- Embeddings/reranker path for retrieval-augmented responses; batch embedding calls for nightly index refresh.

Open questions we flagged:
1) Will the tool-calling step require external network access from the Private cluster? (you mentioned internal API gateway)
2) Desired SLOs for 95th percentile latency on end-to-end flows (including reranker + DB call).
3) Any hard concurrency caps from your side (session token limits / per-IP throttles)?

What we propose (initial):
- Short-term dedicated pool sized to handle sustained 300 concurrent low-latency sessions with burst headroom to 500 for 10–15 minute spikes.
- Autoscale policy: scale in/out on rolling 60s window using queued request depth and 95p token latency signals; cap scale at 8 nodes for initial commit.
- Queueing: front-door request queue with per-customer priority slots and circuit-breaker for backpressure.
- Concurrency per instance: conservative cap at 16 concurrent generation streams per GPU instance with adaptive batching.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx (initial sizing worksheet), and a short playbook appendix.

Next steps / asks for you: 
- Please share a 48–72 hour traffic sample exported to CSV (time-series of requests & latency).
- Confirm whether the internal infra team can allow outbound to our tool-caller endpoints or whether we should plan a Private deployment with VPC egress.

I'll loop Karhtik and Marissa for the technical plan; propose a follow-up on Thursday 12:00 PM ET to finalize capacity numbers.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx (xlsx)]

Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 10:08:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: QoS & throughput plan + next steps

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Tool calling: our payments lookup service is internal-only behind the bank VPC. We cannot allow external outbound from a hosted endpoint; Private deployment (VPC peering or on-prem) is required.
- Latency SLO: End-to-end 95p target is 600ms when cache hit; we can tolerate up to 1.5s for cold hits that trigger reranking + external DB checks.
- Concurrency caps: Security limits per-session are not constraining for now, but infra asks we keep per-instance resource usage predictable (no single instance should exceed 70% GPU memory for safety).

We will export the last 72 hours of traffic and send as a CSV by EOD. Also attaching our gap analysis PDF for context.

— Kate
Kate Reynolds
Director, Product — NovaBank

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: QoS & throughput plan + next steps

Hi all — thanks for the details, Kate. Based on the discovery and the SLOs you quoted, here is a proposed technical approach focused on predictable QoS and safe autoscale: 

1) Private deployment model:
- VPC-hosted control plane with customer-only egress to internal services via VPC peering / Private Service Connect. No external outbound required for tool calling.

2) Sizing assumptions (baseline -> burst):
- 1 GPU node (A100/LLM-optimized) with adaptive batching can sustain ~40 concurrent short-output sessions (avg 400 tokens out) with 95p latency ~500–700ms depending on model.
- Recommendation: initial reserved pool = 8 nodes (est sustained concurrency ~320). Burst buffer 2 additional nodes via autoscale to reach ~480 concurrency for short spikes.

3) Autoscaling & queueing:
- Metric mix: queued request depth (primary), 95p token latency (secondary), and CPU/GPU thermal/headroom signals (safety).
- Scale decision window: 60s lookback, require 2 consecutive windows to expand, single-window for scale-down to avoid flapping.
- Queue policy: per-tenant priority queue with max queue depth 1500; requests beyond threshold return a graceful 429 + Retry-After or route to degraded model variant.

4) Concurrency caps & batching:
- Per-GPU concurrency cap: 16 in the initial profile (fits your 70% memory safety margin). We can tune to 18 if memory usage allows after benchmarking with your prompt corpus.
- Batching: dynamic batching with max batch size 32 and micro-batch timeout 20ms; structured-output tool-calls kept out of token-batching to preserve deterministic call ordering.

5) Embeddings & rerankers:
- Nightly bulk embeddings pipeline for index refresh (batch jobs).
- Reranker: run small dedicated CPU worker pool to score top-N candidates; model hosted on same VPC to avoid cross-network latency.

6) Deliverables I can produce for Thursday's call:
- A revised sizing worksheet with node-level math and cost delta (redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx updated).
- Simple load-generator script and a small benchmark we can run against a non-prod replica of your prompts to validate per-node concurrency.

Ask: Kate — can your infra share an anonymized sample of request/response sizes and the proportion of requests that trigger tool-calls (payments lookup)? That will let us finalize memory & batch config.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

The CSV has timestamp, request_type, payload_size_tokens, response_size_tokens, and observed_latency_ms.

We ran a small non-prod replay at our side and saw that cache-hit flows average 420ms and cold flows with DB calls ~1.1s. We're comfortable with your suggested node caps; infra is okay with Private peering — will start the peering ticket after we align on node counts.
